method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the writing-l4-rules skill; the s 9 hand-over from the executor or administrator to the relatives after 6 months is a regulative rule (PARTY ... DO ... WITHIN ... HENCE FULFILLED LEST PARTY ... MAY) and the seat question reads plain facts; no REFUSE (gaps answer `not covered`, asserted); every finding of the court asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Fatal Accidents Act 1959 (WA), compilation on the Western Australian Legislation website (mrdoc_49105), last amended by the Statutes (Repeals and Minor Amendments) Act 2011 s 5 (in operation 26 October 2011), retrieved 2026-09-07, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_49105.txt. Uncommenced at that compilation: Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Act 2025 Pt 17 Div 8 (not encoded). No regulation sets a number or date this Act uses.

checks.command: l4 run faa-dates.l4 ; l4 run faa-relative.l4 ; l4 run faa-cases-relative.l4
checks.result: 96 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings; 1 #TRACE as its expect line says (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A residual or breached DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so the s 9 rule is asserted through CONSIDER ... WHEN FULFILLED and one residual is #TRACEd.

scope: The whole Act bar machinery: s 3(1) (relative), 3(2)-(4); s 4(1), (2); s 5(1)-(3); s 6(1A), (1B), (2)-(7) (with (3a)); s 7 (and the compilation note keeping the former s 7 for causes of action accrued before 15 November 2005, answered `not covered`); s 8; s 9(1), (2); s 9A(1), (2); s 11; Schedule 2 cl 1. Out: s 1 (short title); s 3(1) 'court' (no answer turns on it); s 9A(3), (4) (procedural orders; other powers saved); the time limit, which is in the Limitation Act 2005.
seat: the relative of the person who died: the family member for whose benefit the action is brought (Schedule 2)
